location.site: former Androscoggin Mill / former paper mill
location.address_note: Riley Road mill property; no parcel-level permit file was located in this refresh.

status_as_of_cutoff: Stalled/on hold as of 2026-08-11; construction was not verified. State records show LD 307 was vetoed and the veto sustained in April 2026 because the bill lacked a Jay carveout, but June 2026 local reporting based on the Jay town manager's statement says Sentinel Data Centers notified JGT2 Redevelopment that it did not intend to move forward at that point. JGT2 was reported to be seeking other interested parties; no replacement operator, local permit, construction start, CO, utility interconnection, energization, or service evidence was located.
evidence_grade: B: official state policy records plus local/town-manager reporting; no primary local permit or utility record located

actions.result_status: Local reporting says Tony McDonald of JGT2 Redevelopment asked the Select Board to support an exemption from LD 307 for the proposed former Androscoggin Mill data center; the board voted to have the town manager work with JGT2 on a letter of support to Governor Mills. This was political/support action, not a site-plan approval or building permit.
actions.vote_tally: reported as board support; exact official minutes not located
actions.access_caveat: Local press report; the official town minutes/letter were not located through web search.
actions.evidence_note: Supports local-process/policy context only; not used to infer approval or construction.

actions.government_body: Office of Governor Janet T. Mills
actions.result_status: Governor Mills vetoed LD 307, a bill that would have created a Maine Data Center Coordination Council and temporarily limited certain data centers, saying she would have signed it if it exempted the project at the former Androscoggin Mill in Jay. The release described the Jay project as a $550 million redevelopment under contract with several permits, but did not identify permit numbers or constitute a local project approval.
actions.access_caveat: Official state policy record; the referenced permits were not itemized in the release and no local permit file was located.
actions.evidence_note: Policy context kept separate from project approval and construction status.

actions.government_body: Office of Governor Janet T. Mills / Maine Legislature
actions.result_status: Governor Mills signed an executive order establishing the Maine Data Center Advisory Council after the Legislature sustained her LD 307 veto; the council is charged with recommendations by January 29, 2027. This did not approve the Jay project.
actions.vote_tally: House override attempt reported elsewhere as 72-65, short of two-thirds
actions.access_caveat: Official policy record; not a project-specific permit or utility approval.
actions.evidence_note: Confirms no statewide moratorium took effect from LD 307, but does not change project physical status.

actions.government_body: Town of Jay status as reported by Maine Public / Sun Journal
actions.result_status: The town manager reported that Sentinel Data Centers notified mill owner JGT2 Redevelopment of its intent not to move forward at that point; JGT2 was pursuing conversations with other interested parties, and the data center project was on hold with future plans undetermined.
actions.access_caveat: Public-radio/local press report of town-manager statement; no signed withdrawal, replacement operator filing, or permit cancellation was located.
actions.evidence_note: Later on-hold evidence is stronger for cutoff status than earlier announcement context.

capacity_note: Developer-reported initial demand from March 2026 local reporting; potential scale higher was conditioned on regional grid review. Because the project is on hold and no interconnection/service record was found, this is proposed demand, not energized load.
owner: JGT2 Redevelopment LLC (reported owner/developer of the former mill site); Sentinel Data Centers was the planned operator/partner but withdrew/notified intent not to move forward in June 2026.

sources.match_reason: Exact Phase3↔regional stable-ID pair; seed merged only with explicit evidence

contradictions.summary: Governor Mills' April 24 official release says the Jay project had received several permits, while March local reporting said the project would not require Jay Planning Board approval or zoning changes because it was inside an existing industrial structure. This refresh did not locate the underlying permit list, permit numbers, building permit, local approval, utility interconnection, CO, or energization record.
